tier_reason: Independent third-party suite wasmi-benchmarks (public harness benches/criterion/startup.rs, runtimes/fizzy/lib.rs; plots in wasmi-labs/wasmi-benchmarks-plots) shows Fizzy at x17.83 startup geomean vs WAMR fast-interpreter x56.73, V8 x33.27, Wasmer Cranelift x1484.15 and Wasmtime Cranelift x1634.19 on an AMD EPYC 7763 (values matched to runtime names by SVG y-coordinate). CPU model and Cargo profile are public but the C++ compiler, its version and the CMake build type used for Fizzy are not stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Startup (compile plus instantiate) geomean relative to the fastest runtime per test (lower is better), AMD EPYC 7763: Fizzy x17.83 vs WAMR fast-interpreter x56.73, V8 x33.27, Wasmer (Cranelift) x1484.15, Wasmtime (Cranelift) x1634.19 (about 3.2x lower than WAMR fast-interp, derived from page data). Fizzy is below WAMR fast-interp on all five CPU data sets (Apple M2 Pro 18.69 vs 49.35, Apple M4 Pro 17.20 vs 43.90, Intel i7-7700 17.63 vs 61.71, Xeon Platinum 8573C 11.21 vs 44.15) and below V8 on four of them, but not on Apple M2 Pro (Fizzy 18.69 vs V8 16.97).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Built by the wasmi-benchmarks harness through Robin Freyler's fizzyx 0.1.1 crate: fizzyx-sys build.rs runs Fizzy's CMake via the Rust cmake crate with FIZZY_TESTING=OFF, FIZZY_WASI=OFF and a force-included compat_shim.hpp; Rust harness profile.bench lto=fat, codegen-units=1. C++ compiler, version and CMake build type are not stated. Fizzy's own README performance setup: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (-O3), LTO, latest GCC or Clang, libstdc++, no -march=native.
corrections.caveats: Startup-only win: on the same suite Fizzy's execution geomean is x45.63 vs WAMR fast-interpreter x17.07, Wasm3 (eager) x16.51 and V8 x1.05 on EPYC 7763 (about 2.7x slower than WAMR fast-interp, derived from page data), so it is not faster than any category baseline at running code. Per-test startup on EPYC: V8 is faster than Fizzy on ffmpeg (35.46 ms vs 215.36 ms), spidermonkey (10.94 ms vs 52.31 ms) and pulldown-cmark (2.30 ms vs 2.72 ms); Fizzy wins on bz2, coremark, argon2 and erc20. Lazy-validating interpreters are far faster at startup (Wasm3 lazy x2.77, Wasmi v2 lazy x1.37). The WAMR comparison is against its fast-interpreter mode, which precompiles at load. Suite is maintained by the author of the competing Wasmi runtime and the Fizzy bindings (fizzyx) are his; plots are regenerated in place (last EPYC update 2026-08-25, values as of 2026-10-06). Fizzy implements WebAssembly 1.0 (MVP) only. Latest commit (2025-11-10) is a README merge; the last code change was 2023-03-03. Fizzy's own CHANGELOG (v0.5.0 detailed results, hardware not stated) shows execution about 5.1x faster than WABT 1.0.19 interpreter (508%) but only 1.7x faster than WABT 1.0.12 (167%), while wasm3 0.4.7 took 26% of Fizzy's execution time and 27% of its instantiation time. Fizzy failed in Frank Denis's libsodium 2021-Q1 run (needs WASI poll_oneoff).

notes: Numbers verified exactly on the EPYC 7763 geomean-startup plot, mapping labels to values by y-coordinate rather than file order. Real but narrow win: startup (parse plus validate plus instantiate) only; execution is about 2.7x slower than WAMR fast-interp and about 43x slower than V8, and V8 beats it on the three largest startup modules and on the M2 Pro geomean. Code dormant since 2023-03; record shortcomings: startup-only, execution slower than every baseline, MVP-only, wrapper written by competing-runtime author.

C compiler and version are not stated (toywasm is built by the toywasmx-sys cc-crate build script), so not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Built by the wasmi-benchmarks harness through Robin Freyler's toywasmx 0.2 crate (features: upstream-default toggles plus tail-call): toywasmx-sys build.rs compiles toywasm with the Rust cc crate, -std=c11, -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=199506L, -DNDEBUG, -fshort-enums; optimisation level from the Cargo bench profile (lto=fat, codegen-units=1). C compiler and version not stated.
corrections.caveats: Startup-only win: on the same suite toywasm's execution geomean is x318.96 vs WAMR fast-interpreter x17.07, Wasm3 (eager) x16.51 and V8 x1.05 on EPYC 7763 (about 18.7x slower than WAMR fast-interp, derived from page data; 128.76 vs 14.77 on Apple M2 Pro). Per-test startup on EPYC: V8 is faster than toywasm on ffmpeg (35.46 ms vs 210.84 ms), spidermonkey (10.94 ms vs 56.01 ms) and pulldown-cmark (2.30 ms vs 2.63 ms). The WAMR comparison is against its fast-interpreter mode, which precompiles at load; the author's own startup.csv (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yamt/toywasm/HEAD/benchmark/startup.csv, MacBook Pro 2018 2.2 GHz 6-core i7) shows WAMR classic interpreter at 0.19 s vs toywasm 0.18 s, wamr fast interp 0.70 s, Wasmtime cached 0.27 s and Wasmtime/Wasmer first run 4.87 s/4.56 s. Wasm3 (lazy) startup is x2.77 on EPYC, far lower. Suite is maintained by the author of the competing Wasmi runtime and the toywasm bindings (toywasmx) are his; plots are regenerated in place, values as of 2026-10-06. Author's own ffmpeg.wasm run (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yamt/toywasm/HEAD/benchmark/ffmpeg.txt, same MacBook, compiler flags not stated): toywasm 65.02 s vs iwasm 2.4.4 classic interpreter 210.58 s (3.2x, derived), WasmEdge 0.17.0 interpreter 198.75 s, wazero interpreter 173.08 s, but slower than wasm3 18.43 s, iwasm fast interpreter 23.14 s and wasmi 29.56 s, and far slower than JIT runtimes (3.54-11.89 s); the README itself says toywasm is slower than Wasm3 and WAMR at execution by design (in-place interpretation).

notes: Numbers verified on the EPYC 7763 geomean-startup plot by y-coordinate, and the all-five-CPUs claim checked (EPYC 18.35 vs V8 33.27; M2 Pro 16.38 vs 16.97; M4 Pro 15.52 vs 21.11; i7-7700 17.59 vs 25.25; Xeon 8573C 10.62 vs 29.21; WAMR fast-interp 43.90-61.71 throughout). Shortcomings to record: startup-only win, execution about 18.7x slower than WAMR fast-interp in the suite, WAMR classic interpreter starts as fast in the author's own data, wrapper written by a competing-runtime author.

tier_reason: Independent third-party libsodium suite by Frank Denis (jedisct1/webassembly-benchmarks 2022-12/res/*.csv, per-test times for wasm2c, Wasmtime, Wasmer, Node, iwasm and native); recomputing the geomeans from the CSVs reproduces every ratio in the record. The results repo states no CPU model, compiler or flags (methodology is in the blocked 00f.net post), so not A; same treatment as the WAVM entry from this suite.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Derived from page data (wasm2c.csv vs the other runtimes' CSVs, geomean of per-test time ratios over the 61 tests that have native results): wasm2c 0.68x Wasmtime, 0.71x Wasmer Cranelift, 0.82x Wasmer LLVM, 0.61x Node/V8, 0.22x Wasmer Singlepass; wasm2c geomean 2.36x native vs Wasmtime 3.46x, Wasmer Cranelift 3.34x, Wasmer LLVM 2.89x, Node 3.91x. Not faster than WAMR: iwasm (AOT per the 2023 post, snippet only) is 2.30x native, wasm2c 1.03x iwasm time, slower on 31 of 61 tests.
corrections.caveats: Not a win over every category baseline: in the same 2022-12 run WAMR iwasm (AOT-compiled per the 00f.net 2023 post, search snippet only) is at par or slightly ahead (wasm2c 1.03x iwasm time geomean over 61 tests, wasm2c slower on 31 of them; iwasm 2.30x native vs wasm2c 2.36x, derived from page data). The results repo (archived 2026-08-19) has no compiler, flags or CPU model for the 2022-12 run (methodology lives in the blocked 00f.net post) and the CSV unit is not stated; lower is better (native lowest, wasm3 highest), so only ratios are used. The native column uses hardware AES on the AEGIS tests (about 74x faster than any Wasm runtime there), which inflates every runtime's x-native geomean equally. Frank Denis's 2026 post (search snippet only, 00f.net blocked) reports wasm2c built with zig cc -O3 -march=native at 0.814x Wasmtime and 0.887x Wasmer geomean with wide_arithmetic, and WAMR AOT at about 1.57x native. The wasm2c C-compile step is not part of the measured time, and the C compiler and flags used to build the wasm2c output in 2022-12 are not public.

notes: All record ratios reproduced exactly from the 12 CSVs (61 common tests). Main shortcoming to record: WAMR iwasm AOT in the same run ties or beats wasm2c (1.03x, 31 of 61 tests slower), so the win is over Wasmtime, Wasmer and V8 only; no CPU or compiler stated in the results repo. Related entry w2c2 (turbolent/w2c2) is a separate Wasm-to-C translator, not a duplicate.
